originality.rationale: The inspected primary 2026 ξ-Bergman paper treats arbitrary-domain construction and an upper-half-plane pure-jet zero-free result, but does not evaluate or count negative-product disk zero fibres. The new claim determines every pure-jet order on the disk using an exact Jacobi reduction. Primary full-text material, published mathematical searches and their stronger-coverage implications were compared. The root properties of Jacobi/Legendre are acknowledged classical inputs, not claimed as innovations; unindexed equivalents remain a concrete risk.
residual_risks: Classical special-function literature may contain equivalent identities for these hypergeometric numerators, and an unindexed direct disk jet-kernel calculation may predate this result.
The inspected parent paper is a readable full-text mirror of the preprint rather than directly downloaded arXiv PDF; mathematical section coverage was materially checked.

source_inspections.assessment: Establishes the canonical construction for any domain; computes pure-jet kernel and zero-freeness for H, not the unit disk. A full-domain theorem transporting ordinary jets would not be valid without accounting for derivative mixing.
evidence: §§2–3 define and derive the canonical positive-definite two-variable Gram kernel and normalized ξ-jet evaluations.
§4 Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.5 specialize explicitly to H; Theorem 4.11 says H is ξ-Lu Qi-Keng for ξ=δ_N.
Full-text searches for disk/disc/Jacobi found no relevant disk zero-fibre classification; §§5–6 address H boundary behavior and covariance.

§6 Remark 6.3 explicitly shows that a single-coordinate pure jet transforms to a base-point-dependent sequence with lower coordinates, so the H result cannot simply be transported as a pure jet on the disk.

value.rationale: A single-coordinate differential sequence is the canonical simplest nontrivial object in the newly proposed ξ-Bergman Gram family. Determining all orders on the disk and the exact number of negative-product zero fibres is a natural complete Lu Qi-Keng classification, exposes a sharp geometric contrast with the already-proved upper-half-plane case, and may be used as a benchmark for mixed jets. No unsupported claim of a general mixed-jet theorem is made.
